Executive Order 14074 established federal measures on misconduct data, independent investigation of in-custody deaths, profiling safeguards, use-of-force standards, and public reporting (E007). The administration also supported gun-safety legislation addressing background checks, trafficking, school safety, and behavioral-health programs (E009), while federal officials issued protest-response guidance emphasizing de-escalation and peaceful assembly (E030). Against this, civil-society reviewers judged the policing order an important but insufficient foundation, dependent on implementation (E008), and the Justice Department opened a pattern-or-practice investigation into the NYPD's treatment of sexual-assault survivors and gender-biased policing (E044). Those findings document serious local protection failures, but not a completed nationwide outcome or a presidentially directed pattern. Later federal database implementation is contextual rather than a 2022 outcome (E021). The severity class is recurring and selective institutional failure, not widespread or systematic repression.
